This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.609/2017 on the file of the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Thalassery, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 07/12/2019.

sentences.text: The respondents herein are respondents 1 to 4 respectively in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 18/04/2016 at about 06:45 p.m., while he was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KL.20.B.2463 and when he reached the place by name Manjakkal Thodu at Ponniam, car bearing registration no.KL.01.R.8812 driven by deceased E.M.Nanu in a rash and 2025:KER:59768 MACA NO. 345 OF 2020 negligent manner knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
A sum of 1,00,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.

3. Respondents 1 to 3, the legal heirs of deceased E.M.Nanu, remained ex parte.
4.
The fourth respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy in respect of the offending vehicle, but denied negligence on the part of the deceased.
It was also contended that the compensation claimed was quite excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A13 and Ext.X1 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No evidence was adduced by the fourth respondent/insurer.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides,
found negligence on the part of deceased who drove the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 36,56,640/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date 2025:KER:59768 MACA NO. 345 OF 2020 of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

8. Heard both sides Rajul P.C vs Girija on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191417843/
2 9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner - Notional income

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that though an amount of 20,000/- was claimed as the monthly income, the Tribunal has fixed the notional income at 18,000/- only which is quite low as the claim petitioner was a 4th semester student of Mechatronics.
Therefore, the Tribunal ought to have fixed the monthly income as 20,000/-.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the fourth respondent/insurer that the 2025:KER:59768 MACA NO. 345 OF 2020 notional income that has been fixed is on the higher side and therefore the same needs to be appropriately reduced.
9.1. Though it is submitted that the income fixed is on the higher side, no appeal or cross objection has been filed by the fourth respondent/insurer.

Taking into account the qualification of the claim petitioner and the fact that he was a bright student which was noticed by the Tribunal in the impugned Award, I find that the amount of 18,000/- fixed as monthly income is just and reasonable and that it does not call for any interference by this Court.
Addition to be made towards future prospects 10.
The claim petitioner was aged 19 years at the time of the incident.
The disability has been assessed as 78%.
Therefore, 40% of his established income is liable to be added towards future prospects while computing compensation for permanent disability.
Future treatment 11. IA No.1 of 2025 filed by the claim petitioner for 2025:KER:59768 MACA NO. 345 OF 2020 receiving additional documents is partly allowed.
The documents referred to as Annexures I and II are admitted in evidence and marked as Ext.A14 series.
As per Ext.A14 series, an amount of 33,500/- was expended for replacing the lost teeth and 71,000/- is stated to be the estimate of the expenses for future treatment.
The claim petitioner is entitled to the said amounts under this head.
Loss of amenities 12.
It is pointed out that though an amount of 4,00,000/- was claimed under this head, the Tribunal has granted an amount of 40,000/- only.
The learned counsel for the claim petitioner submitted that this is a meagre amount taking into account the injuries sustained and the resultant disability caused to the claim petitioner.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the fourth respondent/insurer that the amount of 40,000/- granted is quite reasonable and no further enhancement is called for.

sentences.text: 5 15.10.2016: EXPLORATION & TRANSFER OF RIGHT SAN TO RIGHT SSN (POSTERIOR APPROACH).
Under GA, patient was in left lateral position, right neck and scapular region painted and draped adequately.

A oblique incision (16cm) was given over spine of right scapula, with meticulous dissection spine of scapula was exposed, right trapezius muscle was resected from the spine of scapula and retracted proximally.
Dissection done through the superior border 2025:KER:59768 MACA NO. 345 OF 2020 of scapula, scapulo-humeral ligament found and cut.
Supra-scapular nerve was found in suprascapular notch and cut in adequate length.
Then dissection done medially, SAN was found underneath trapezius muscle and cut in adequate length as much as possible.
Then SAN was sutured with SSN by 10-0 ethilon under microscope.
Wound closure done in layers..
Skin closure done by 3- 0 ethilon.
Right arm was strapped with chest.
Condition at Discharge Patient is comfortable.
Dressing changed.
Suture lines dry.
Advice on discharge Maintain the position of right upper limb.
Maintain arm pouch.
Suture removal after 10 days.
Electrical stimulation and physiotherapy has not start after 1 month."
(Emphasis supplied)

In the light of the injury sustained and the disability hereinabove referred to and taking into account the fact that the claim petitioner was only 19 years old at the time of the incident, I find that an amount of 2,00,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
Loss of marriage prospects 13.
Though the learned counsel for the claim petitioner 2025:KER:59768 MACA NO. 345 OF 2020 submits that disfiguration was caused, there are no materials on record to establish the same.
However, taking into account the fact that the claim petitioner was only aged 19 years at the time of the accident, an amount of 50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
